page: Microsoft Azure FX64-32ms_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. This instance features 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache. The server is highly memory-optimized, providing 1344.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 42.0 GB of memory per physical core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data shows top-tier single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core, image processing, and text processing scores placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Large-block memory bandwidth (both read and write) is also strong, placing in the top 25%. For language model workloads, prompt processing speeds for small and medium models are strong, though text generation for large 70B models falls into the bottom 25% due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX64-32ms_v2 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a specialized option for memory-bound workloads. The high clock speed of 4.2 GHz provides strong single-threaded performance, offsetting the lower total core count compared to other high-memory instances. However, the absence of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on external network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs.

This server configuration is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require high single-core CPU speeds. Suitable workloads include large in-memory databases, memory-bound enterprise applications, data processing pipelines, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing.
